title: instanceof against an ancestor of the declared parameter type is always true

ground_truth.statement: Exception is in RuntimeException's parent chain and instanceof walks the chain, so `$e instanceof \Exception` is true for every value the parameter can hold and the expression cannot distinguish any two inputs.

psalm.reason: Psalm 6.20.0 does not require RedundantCondition on a bare returned instanceof expression. Its standalone InstanceofAnalyzer assigns bool; conditional reconciliation is a separate reporting context. This exclusion concerns warning scope, not whether the expression is semantically always true.

mago.reason: Mago 1.57.0 infers literal true for this subtype test but does not emit redundant-condition on a bare returned instanceof. Its own parent-class fixture permits this expression without a diagnostic. Missing a warning here is a reporting-scope divergence, not failed subtype reasoning.

notes: The first benchmark draft incorrectly counted Psalm and Mago silence as FN by requiring a warning on every constant Boolean expression. Version-pinned source and tests show different diagnostic scopes. Their rows are excluded from the denominator with citations. The companion redundant-instanceof-in-condition tests an actual conditional context separately.
